title: Rooming with Cootie Williams in segregated hotels
summary: On Goodman's tours Maxwell registers for both of them in Ohio hotels; Cootie declines to make trouble.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Like when we were with Benny Goodman, joined the band. Well, I generally liked to room alone but we would get into a place like Ohio or someplace

and they wouldn't have any place for Cootie to stay. So I would check in in both our names and then Cootie would come in the room. And it broke my heart the first time he said, "You check in and I'll carry the bags in and act like I'm the band-boy." I said, "Bullshit. I'll check in and you walk in and I'll carry my own bags." That much I'll do.

So then he didn't want to go down to the dining room and he said, "We'll have room service." So I didn't want to go out and eat and leave him alone so it cost me a lot of money. But the first time I said, "Look, we'll go down to the dining room, you don't have to do anything. If they say anything at all, I'll pop them, you know." And he said, "No, I don't want to make any trouble and I don't want to embarrass you, embarrass the band. Leave it alone, it's all right."
So I know the feeling, that he just didn't want to put me on the spot.
Sure, it could be quite inconvenient and embarrassing on both sides.
